synthesizedFacts.fact: Sun damage can lead to uneven pigmentation due to increased melanin production, resulting in conditions like solar lentigines and melasma.
Solar ultraviolet radiation (UVR) exposure is a significant risk factor for skin damage, leading to conditions such as sunburn, actinic keratosis, and skin cancers.
Sun exposure can cause both acute and chronic skin reactions, including immunosuppressive skin diseases and photoallergic reactions.
People with darker skin have more natural protection against sun damage due to higher melanin content, but they are still susceptible to sun damage.
